subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: After transaction-authoritative authorization is fixed, should plugin-runtime callers permanently fail closed on legacy ownerless session rows, or should OpenClaw provide an explicit ownership migration or adoption path?
rationale: The current atomicity defect is mechanical, but treatment of previously persisted ownerless rows is a compatibility-sensitive plugin authorization policy that tests cannot decide.

options.title: Fail closed
options.body: Reject plugin-runtime mutation of ownerless rows and document that operators or non-plugin clients must manage or replace them.

options.title: Migrate ownership
options.body: Provide a doctor or operator workflow that assigns a verified plugin owner before plugin-runtime mutation is permitted.

recommendation.title: Fail closed
recommendation.body: Reject plugin-runtime mutation of ownerless rows and document that operators or non-plugin clients must manage or replace them.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history ties this person to both the session patch accessor and the existing delete ownership boundary.
